$comment: THE CATALOGUE OF THINGS YOU CAN BUILD. Authored like the action catalogue:
curated, versioned, and never renamed once shipped.
WHAT IS FROZEN HERE IS THE `id`, AND ONLY THE id. It appears inside spend
events forever, so an item may be retired but never renamed and never reused
for a different thing. Everything else on the line is presentation or tuning.
*Corrected 2026-09-01: the v1 header of this file said `slot` was frozen too.
That was an over-claim written while the room had twelve fixed boxes. A cell
is not stored in any event — it is where the renderer puts the sprite — so
rearranging the room is a layout change, not a data migration. Freezing it
would have meant the room could never be redecorated, which is the opposite
of the product.*
PRICE IS TUNABLE for the same reason grants are (ADR-012): the resolved cost
is stored on the spend event at purchase time, so a 2031 rebalance cannot make
a 2026 purchase cost more, or less, than it did.
PRICING, per ECONOMY.md §3: the first item in a room costs about ONE GOOD
WEEK, not one good day. At ~130 Embers a day that is ~900. An upgrade you can
afford the day you unlock it teaches the player that the currency is
meaningless, and that lesson is not recoverable. tests.js enforces the floor.
SKILL POINTS GATE, EMBERS PAY. `unlock_level` is read against the skill-tree
level from Character.build() — permission, not payment. A locked item is
always VISIBLE: seeing what is ahead is the reward, and a shop that hides what
you have not earned reads as a shop that thinks you are behind.
EVERY SKILL HAS AN ENTRY ITEM AT unlock_level 1. ADR-020 applied to spending:
a tree you can fill but never spend from is a locked tree with extra steps.
LAYOUT. The room is a grid of 16-pixel tiles. Rows 0-3 are wall (row 3 is the
wainscot band), rows 4-9 are floor. An item names its top-left `cell` and its
`size` in tiles; `layer` decides draw order — rug, then floor, then wall.
Placement is FIXED for now, not player-chosen: free placement is a later slice
and changes nothing about the ledger when it arrives, because a position would
be a field on the spend event, which §2.6 already permits with no migration.
SIX FLOOR CELLS ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT EMPTY. They draw as faint outlines, so
the room reads as 'there is room for more' rather than 'you have nothing' —
the same reason a locked item stays visible in the shop.
ART. Sprites are 16x16 pixel grids in tiles.js, which is the swap seam: a
bought tileset (Kenney CC0, LimeZu Modern Interiors) replaces that one module
with one returning spritesheet slices under the same names, and nothing here
changes. `sprite` is a name in that module, never a file path.

fixtures.note: Never bought, never lost. The room is never empty on day one.

items.label: A woven rug
items.blurb: The floor stops being a floor.

items.label: A door worth knocking on
items.blurb: Someone could arrive at it.

items.label: A stove that works
items.blurb: Both rings, every time.

items.label: A desk of your own
items.blurb: You can leave things half-finished on it.

items.label: Something green
items.blurb: It only needs you about once a week.

items.label: A bed worth getting into
items.blurb: And, on the bad days, worth getting out of.

items.label: A mat at the door
items.blurb: The bit that says someone lives here.

items.label: A nightstand and a lamp
items.blurb: Somewhere for the water glass and the pills.

items.label: A lamp on the wall
items.blurb: Warmer than the overhead light, and kinder at night.

items.label: Something on the wall
items.blurb: You chose it. That is the whole point of it.

items.label: A sink with hot water
items.blurb: Dishes stop being a project.

items.label: A shelf for your things
items.blurb: Everything gets a place that is its own.

items.label: A table to eat at
items.blurb: Sitting down to it is the whole point.

items.label: A chair for someone else
items.blurb: It can stay empty. It is still theirs.

items.label: A clock that ticks
items.blurb: Quiet rooms are better with one sound in them.

items.label: An armchair by the fire
items.blurb: Facing the hearth, because of course it is.

items.label: The window with morning light
items.blurb: East-facing. It does most of the work.

items.label: A rack of good tools
items.blurb: Sharp, hung up, and where you left them.

items.label: Curtains that actually close
items.blurb: You decide when it is morning.

items.label: A shelf of books
items.blurb: Some of them you have even read.

items.label: A stocked pantry
items.blurb: There is always something in it.

items.label: A second lamp
items.blurb: Now the corners are lit too.

items.label: Counter you can work on
items.blurb: Room to put the board down and actually cook.

items.label: A wardrobe
items.blurb: Clean clothes live here, not on the chair.

items.label: A proper workbench
items.blurb: The vice alone changes what you can attempt.

items.label: A sofa to sink into
items.blurb: Long enough to lie down on.
